lapses.what: t1's second acceptance criterion, which I wrote, is not literally computable: it asks for the stricter of the start-time and the decision-time mode in exactly the case where the start time is UNKNOWN, so there is no start-time mode to compare. The task agent resolved it by treating the unknowable side as worst-case strict -- which is right, and matches c5 and the clock-trust rule -- but it is an interpretation of an ambiguous criterion, not a mechanical implementation of what the criterion says. The agent flagged it rather than smoothing it over; the lapse is mine for writing a criterion whose own terms do not apply to its case.

lapses.what: My first test for Qodo finding 4 PASSED and was VACUOUS. It asserted that the injected mode and the speech-start mode were both 'weekday' at a chosen instant -- but the host's own resolver returns weekday at most instants, so the assertion held whether or not the fix existed. I only found it because I ran the negative control, which passed when it should have failed. Rewritten to assert IDENTITY (the injected object itself is what both readings return), which fails correctly without the fix. The lesson is the day's own rule applied to myself twice over: a test that passes is not evidence until it has been shown it can fail.
